scientific_intent.scientific_task: Evaluate a generalized plasmon-pole self-energy summation at three frequencies
scientific_intent.mathematical_operation: Sum complex rational pole factors times inverse-dielectric and conjugated band-amplitude products over bands, owned reciprocal vectors and plane waves; six scalar Float64 atomic reductions.
scientific_intent.discretization: Four finite small band/reciprocal-index cases, three frequencies 3/4/5, source uniform and varied signed dyadic complex coefficients, nonidentity inverse map and exact-zero control.
scientific_intent.accuracy_requirements: Full six output scalars against independent Decimal80 allterm oracle at predeclared 1e-11+1e-11|gold|; all input bits/guards exact, both GPU references checked on every trial.
scientific_intent.input_size_regime: (nb,ng,nc)=(3,2,31),(5,3,67),(7,4,129),(2,1,1), includes partial warp and grid-stride loops; not source512-band default or 32768-plane-wave benchmark.
scientific_intent.precision_sensitivity: Float64 complex arithmetic and unordered atomic accumulation; nonsingular denominator>=7.3916, total complex condition<=7.55; no resonant/singular pole accuracy or general physical error bound.
scientific_intent.community_use_case: Self-energy miniapplication extracted from BerkeleyGW electronic excited-state/material calculations. This is a kernel operator study, not a physical quasiparticle prediction or complete BerkeleyGW validation.
scientific_intent.description: Preserve unchanged native AoS and historical genuine CUDA.jl SoA operators. New independent full-frequency checker replaces original first-frequency one-sided host checker. Portable versions keep per-thread accumulators/grid-stride loops and six Float64 atomics.
scientific_intent.provenance: Repository README gpp description and MIT2019NERSC native sources. Primary background: Vergara Larrea et al., CUG2019 Experiences Porting Mini-applications..., https://cug.org/proceedings/cug2019_proceedings/includes/files/pap137s2-file1.pdf sections introduction/GPP identify BerkeleyGW General Plasmon Pole self-energy summation; no new material-science prediction claim.
